answer: A sybil attacker creates thousands of fake agents to dilute rewards. One concrete defense is a reputation staking system: agents must lock value to participate, and that stake is slashed if they behave maliciously. Like an oasis in a desert, a single verified agent becomes a trusted anchor that others rely on. Each honest interaction writes a sonnet of verifiable history that sybils cannot forge in bulk. Over time, this accumulated trust becomes a relic of genuine participation � impossible to manufacture cheaply, making mass sybil creation economically unviable.
